title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the 2020 Committee report sets out how it will put AI standards in place to protect public interests. It outlines plans to create clear guidelines, promote transparency, and work with industry to ensure AI is safe, fair, and beneficial for society.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual explains how it will regulate the use of artificial intelligence in qualifications to keep exams fair and trustworthy. The policy sets clear rules for when and how AI can be used in creating and marking assessments, ensuring transparency and accountability.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted material is used to train AI systems, evaluating the legal, economic, and ethical implications of that practice. It offers an impact assessment and recommends policy measures to balance creators’ rights with AI innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” acknowledging the urgent need for stronger AI regulation and investment. It outlines a plan to boost research, enhance public trust, and address ethical, safety, and economic challenges posed by artificial intelligence.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of the committee that will review how artificial intelligence interacts with public standards, including key questions it will address. It also provides a FAQ section that explains the committee’s objectives, membership, processes, and what it aims to achieve.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the UK Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission stresses the need for clear regulations, transparency, and accountability to ensure AI technologies are safe, ethical, and beneficial for society.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explores how artificial intelligence will change the rules and oversight of medical products, addressing new challenges and opportunities for safety and effectiveness. It also lays out a practical plan for putting the AI White Paper principles into action, so that developers and regulators can work together to keep medical AI products reliable, transparent, and compliant.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to position our military as the leading AI‑enabled force for a nation of our size, prioritising effectiveness, efficiency, trustworthiness, and influence. It outlines our commitment to developing advanced AI capabilities that support national security objectives and enhance operational excellence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport AI Action Plan shows how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to use AI to improve services, safety, and efficiency. It also outlines measures to address risks and protect privacy and security.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report explains how copyright‑protected works are currently being used to train AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act, detailing the progress made and the methods employed. It also discusses the legal challenges, compliance requirements, and possible future directions for balancing copyright protection with AI development.
